utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning, Madam Registrar. Will you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning, everyone. This is case number IT-05-88-T, the Prosecutor versus Vujadin Popovic et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes. Good morning, everybody. All the accused are here. From the Defence teams, I notice the absence of Mr. Bourgon and Mr. Haynes. Prosecution, we have present Mr. McCloskey and Mr. Vanderpuye. Yes, any preliminaries? None. So I see that contact is already established. Mr. Blagojevic, dobar dan.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You are about to start giving evidence very shortly. You've been brought forward as a witness by one of the accused here, Colonel Vujadin Popovic; and before you start your testimony, our law requires that you make a solemn declaration to the effect, that in the course of your testimony, you will be speaking the truth. I understand that you have been handed a copy of the text of the solemn declaration already. Please read it out aloud, and that will be your solemn undertaking with us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. Please make yourself comfortable. Lead counsel for Popovic will now introduce himself to you and start with his questions. Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Blagojevic. I am Zoran Zivanovic. I appear for Vujadin Popovic in this case. Would you kindly give us your full name for the record.

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Good morning. I am Nedo, son of Milos, Blagojevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Would you please give us the place and date of your birth.

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: 13th February 1955, Micevici village, municipality Lukavac, the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, Socialist Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Tell us about your educational attainment.

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: I completed primary school, higher school of engineering in Lukavac, and the military academy land forces, as well as the quarter-master services school in Belgrade, the vocation of communications.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us whether you joined the Yugoslav People's Army; and if so, when?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: I joined the Yugoslav People's Army on the 14th September 1974, when I enrolled -- in fact, when I graduated from the military academy --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: When I enrolled in military academy because completion of military academy counts as completed regular military service.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And the military academy is a four-year course.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you ever join the Army of Republika Srpska; and if so, when?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: I joined the Army of Republika Srpska immediately as soon as it was established; that was sometime in May 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, in which unit of the VRS did you service?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: At the time, I was in the communications unit of the Drvar Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And later, did you transfer to the Drina Corps; and if so, when?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: I joined the Drina Corps when it was established. They needed a chief of communications and I was appointed to that position, but the official date of establishment of the Drina Corps was the 1st of November, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you continue in this position in the Drina Corps all the time?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: I was in that position from that date until the end of the war and even further on until 1997, when I retired.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: What was your rank?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: When I took up my position I was a major. In 1995, I was promoted to lieutenant-colonel and I was retired in that rank.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: You said you were chief of communications. I would then like to ask you: What were the responsibilities of the chief of communications in the corps?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: The responsibilities of the chief of communications in the corps were to organize, establish, plan, and maintain communications established.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: As chief of communications, can you tell me to whom were you directly subordinated?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: The chief of communications with his organ of communications was situated in the headquarters of the command of the Drina Corps; his immediate superior was Chief of Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Does that mean that you could receive orders from the Chief of Staff?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Well, I mostly received them from the Chief of Staff and only exceptionally from the corps commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: In the Drina Corps, was there a communications battalion?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: In the Drina Corps, like in other corps, there was a unit for maintaining communications with other units and that was the communications battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you recall who was the commander of that battalion?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Well, from the beginning until 1995, the commander of the communications battalion was Milenko Jevdjevic; he was later promoted and left this position in the rank of major.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Were you able, as chief of communications, to issue orders to that battalion?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: I, as chief of communications, was not able to give orders directly to the commander of that battalion. I could only exceptionally pass on orders from the corps commander to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: What is the relationship of the chief of communications with that communications unit; that is, your relationship with this communications unit?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Well, based on the plan of communications and the orders I received from the Chief of Staff, I had to control and verify the implementation of these plans of communications and to check how communications were established.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, were there any communications units in specific units?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Every brigade, according to establishment, had to have a communications company, larger or smaller. At any rate, each unit had its own subunit for communications to maintain communications with superiors and with other units.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, from your recollection, what type of communications equipment did the Drina Corps have at that time, or more precisely 1995?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Compared to the very beginning, in 1995 we were better equipped in terms of communications. We had a group of radio devices, radio relay devices, telephone and telegraph devices, and encryption devices. Among radio devices, we had more powerful devices, Radio Teletypes 400, Radio Teletype 100, RUP-33 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can you slow the witness down, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I haven't received interpretation of what Mr. Zivanovic said.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Mr. Zivanovic was just repeating what I asked, to slow down. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Blagojevic, it's important that you slow down a little bit because the interpreters have to catch up with you. Mr. Zivanovic, thank you for intervening and please proceed with your questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you continue, please. We stopped in our record with radio Teletype 400, Radio Teletype 100, and RUP-33. Maybe you could repeat all these devices again, because of your speed the interpreters missed something.

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Take it more slowly.

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Radio Teletype system 400, Radio Teletype system 100, RUP-3 and RUP-33, RUP-12. Those are radio devices. Now I'm talking about radio relay devices: FM 200, RRU-800, and RRU-1. Out of telephone devices, we had VZ12K, TC 40, TC 10, and TC 12 or sometimes called TCI 20, and Telephones F 63. We also had interphones.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you just repeat, we couldn't hear one bit very clearly. You said TC 10, and after that?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: TC 40, I said first; then TC 10 -- or TLC 10 and TLC 20, because TLC is an older version.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you remember radio relay equipment that you have -- that you had? I didn't notice it in the enumeration, but maybe I missed it.

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: I noted them after radios. Radio relays, we had FM 200, RRU-800, and RRU-1.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us, briefly, about the features of telecommunications available with RUP-12?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Radio devices RUP-12, like all radios, provide circular communication in all directions horizontally. The range is about ten kilometres; and with good visibility, it can be even 15 or up to 20. It's 30 to 70 megahertz; that is the frequency range which is adjustable.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us, briefly, the characteristics of RRU-1?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Radio relay device RRU-1, unlike radio devices, provides communication in one direction and has one channel through which it can communicate both speech and typed text. Professionally, we call it telegraphy, and that's why on our schemes we always marked it TLF for telephony and TLG for telegraphy. The frequency range is somewhere between 230 and 270 megahertz.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you just tell me another thing, characteristics of RRU-800.

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: The radio relay devices of this type, just like RRU-1, provides communication in one direction, but the 800 conveys a group of channels in its relay beam, depending on multiplex devices with greater frequency plugged into it. It can communicate from four to 24 channels. Usually, you communicate four, eight, 12, or 24 channels in the scale -- on this scale.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And do you remember the frequency range of these devices?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Well, radio relay devices RRU-800 operated within a frequency range of 600 to 900 megahertz.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Now would you kindly tell me - and we will stay on the radio relay device RRU-800 - do you remember about the radio relay route from the base of the corps in Vlasenica to the brigades? What was the layout of that route towards the brigade of Zvornik; the Zvornik Brigade, not just any brigade?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: The radio relay route for communications between the corps and the Zvornik Brigade went from Vlasenica to Veliki Zep; Velika Zep-Cer; and Cer-Gucevo; and Gucevo-Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Did this route exist specifically in July 1995?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. This route did not change from beginning to end because there was no need to change it, so it was in place in July 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you recall another direction of RRU-800 which worked from the command of the Drina Corps in Vlasenica, on one hand, and the subordinates in brigades, on the other hand? I'm talking again about July 1995?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: There was a communication through the RRU-800 with the command of the 2nd Romanija that went through Veliki Zep and devices RRU-800 in Sokolac; although, the command of the 2nd Marina was further on -- 2nd Romanija was further on. There was also connection with the Rogatica Brigade through Veliki Zep.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And how was communication maintained with other units with which there was no RRU communication?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: As for the Bratunac Brigade, we could not have direct communication either from Veliki Zep or from any other hub; rather, we used RRU-1 at Veliki Zep in order to maintain communication with the Bratunac Brigade. And, again, from Veliki Zep where there was an RRU-1, we maintained connection with the DG Pribicevac on Pribicevac hill and in Pribicevac village; and also with the manoeuvre brigade in the village of Kozluk. From Veliki Zep, through RRU-1, we maintained communication with the manoeuvre brigade in Kozluk.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, when we're talking about the communications that were maintained with RRU-800, were these communications routes protected, were they safe? We're talking about RRU-80 and RRU-8 [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Most of the communication was not safe, it was not secured; however, the telegrams were encrypted or protected in popular words, in layman's terms. Because as soon as the corps command was established, I was the head of communications and head of encryption, and I issued an order that all communication about combat activities should be encrypted and sent via a written document. In other words, it has to be done securely. This is what was done because I insisted on that procedure.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: What you have just told us now, what device were you talking about because there's some ambiguities in the record?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Both RRU-1 and RRU-800.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Were there devices for encrypting speech for these devices?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: For RRU-800, there was no device to provide group protection. It was only possible to single out one channel, which was only applied on RRU-1, and that's KZU 61. It could protect one channel in the speech area, which we applied towards the tactical group Pribicevac in June 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember, and you told us what was the radio relay route between Vlasenica and Zvornik, do you remember were there in addition to the RRU-800 there was another device that was operational on any one of the parts of that route?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: From the command of the Drina Corps to Veliki Zep, we had two relay routes: One was with FM 200 and the other was with RRU-800. From Veliki Zep to Cer, we had an SMC device which had a larger capacity of channels than any other devices at our disposal, and it had a much higher frequency that was not so easy to intercept. It was much harder. As for the rest, on other parts of the route between Veliki Zep, Cer, and Zvornik, we had nothing but RRU-800 devices.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me about SMC device, what was its frequency range? Do you remember? Was that frequency range different than all the others that you've just talked about?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: The SMC device, unlike RRU-800 whose frequency was between 600 and 900 megahertz, the SMC had a frequency range from 4.4 to 4.6 gigahertz and from 4.8 to 5.0 gigahertz. It worked in two parts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Zivanovic, ask him to slow down a little bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Blagojevic, let me just remind you, could you please slow down a little in order to help the interpreters interpret your words correctly.

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: If need be, I will repeat.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, then, repeat the last thing. Just give us the frequencies that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't think there is a need for him to repeat. We have it all, but I got the feeling that he was running too fast.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I apologise. You don't have to repeat, sir. Please tell me what measures you, as the chief of communications in 1995, in the summer of that year, what measures did you take in order to better protect your communication from possible interception? I'm talking about RRU-100 [as interpreted] and RRU-1 devices.

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: When I was talking about the protection of communication, on the eve of the operation at Srebrenica, at RRU-1 at Pribicevac, I mounted a KZU 61 to protect speech as well, and there had already been protection of written information there. I had an encrypting machine at the command post as well. As for radio device RUP-12, I mounted a KZU 3 [as interpreted] so that the radio communication also had a protected speech, secured speech, communication.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell me, you're talking about Veliki Zep. Can you describe what it was that was on Veliki Zep? What was the feature there? What was the building there or what kind of a centre?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Veliki Zep was the main radio relay hub of the Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska, and it was also the same thing for the command of the Drina Corps because we did not have any means to establish our own hub. Veliki Zep was suitable to be the hub of the Drina Corps as well. The terrain lended itself perfectly for that function.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Zivanovic, I want to understand better. Referring to his previous answer, not this last one, when he said Pribicevac, he mounted a KZU 61, and for radio device RUP-12, he mounted a KZU 3 to secure communications. Were these kind of scrambling machines or what, scramble devices or what? If he could describe how they protected speech communication, these two pieces of equipment.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: You heard the President's question. You understood, I suppose, so could you please answer.

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: KZU 61, when I was talking, maybe it was too fast. I mounted that to protect speech on the relay route for RRU-1; and as for the operations, when it came to RUP-12 radio-sets, that's where I mounted the KZU 63 to protect speech as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What I want to know as well --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe I was clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. But what I want to know, Mr. Blagojevic, is how these two pieces of equipment, the KZU 61 and KZU 63, protected speech. What was their effect? How would speech communication be protected by their use? Did they scramble speech communication or what?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With RUP-12, which doesn't have a KZU 63, you can't hear a thing from the device that has a KZU 63; complete protection. And KZU 61 on a relay device scrambles, distorts speech; it distorts it to the point of not being intelligible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I showed you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. Sorry, again, Mr. Zivanovic. But in the case of an RUP-12 using a KZU 63 device, you say you have complete protection; you cannot hear a thing. But if you are communicating with someone at the other end, how would that person on the other end be able to hear what you are saying, if with the KZU 63 you have complete protection and you don't hear a thing? In other words, does the person on the receiving end, does he require to have special equipment to receive the communication when it's passing through a KZU 63 device?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Every combat activity or group that participated in Operation Srebrenica had a RUP-12 with a KZU 63 that I personally mounted on that device, so that it was possible to communicate for all the combat groups between themselves and the command of the combat task that was located in Pribicevac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. So, my final question to you: Do you confirm to me that there was no means at the time, no technical means at the time, by which one could intercept a communication between RUP-12 machines with a KZU 63 device mounted?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correct. It was impossible to intercept or listen in to any of those conversations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Let's just clarify a little bit more. An interlocutor who would be using a KZU 63, what would the other interlocutor have to have in order to hear him, i.e., to be able to understand what the first person was saying? What does the other interlocutor have to have at his disposal?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: In order for somebody who's not in the network of RUP-12 devices, to be able to hear what is being said in the network supplied with a KZU 63, he would have the same KZU 63 on an RUP-12. However, a certain key has to be inserted into that other KZU 63, so the device itself is not enough. You have to have a numerical key that consists of several digits, more than one digit, and that has to be inserted into that KZU 63 device.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Does that mean that somebody who wanted to listen in to such a conversation would have to have both the device and several -- and the several-digit key?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: The same key, not just any, the same key, the same device. Yes. If they had that, they would be able to intercept and listen in to the conversations.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I've shown you the expert opinion provided by Mr. Djuro Rodic, and I'm going to ask you about several details of that analysis. Could you please look at the binder that has been presented to you. You will find it under number 3. On page 22, there is an image, a scheme. This is 1D323 and page 22, attachment 53. It's a schematic.

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please hold on just for a second for the image to appear on our screens as well.

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Before the image appears on your screen, Mr. Zivanovic, could you please explain things to me. Everything I have is in English. What is this? I need your explanation.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I can see, this is an antenna for RRU-800. I suppose you are able to recognise this?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that. That's okay, but everything is in English. Why am I looking at this?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Unfortunately, there has been a mistake. I've not been able to locate the original analysis in e-court; and since I'll be asking you about the image only, I believe that in this case you will be able to recognise what the thing is all about without being able to understand the words. My question is this: Could you please explain what is this? What are we looking at here?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: This is an antenna for RRU-800, and the same one is for the 200 device. Let me explain. This is the antenna holder which has up to eight parts. There are two radio -- antenna radiators on the top; and here on the side --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Stop for one moment. Sorry to interrupt you like this, Mr. Blagojevic. Mr. Zivanovic, from what I can gather, Mr. Blagojevic is pointing to the diagram that he has in front of him, but we can't see what he's pointing at from that diagram.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Blagojevic, we cannot see what you are pointing at. I don't know whether there are any technical possibilities to have that shown to us. I'm going to ask you just one thing. I'm going to rephrase my question a little. I just want to ask you to tell us --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Ultimately, Mr. Zivanovic, because let's be practical. In relation to this diagram, what is the purpose of your question or your series of questions? What do you want to establish?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I would like for him to establish the name of two devices at the very top of the antenna.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. You mean to say where there is reflector and radiator?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. And my question is if he could confirm that such a position of the radiator was the same as at the place, at the site --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Then go --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: -- straight to those questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And I am told that the only way, "technical" if you can so call it, that we can go about it is for the witness to mark the document that he has in front of him; and then it will be brought over here and we can see it later on, but I don't think this is the optimum.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So, if the purpose of your question is what you said, I think you can address the witness straight to the top of that diagram where you have those two pieces, those two devices, and you ask the questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell us, what are the two things or devices that you see at the very top of the antenna pole?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: On the top of the antenna pole are radiators. It says reflector or radiator here; but if you pay a closer attention, you will see that there are actually two radiators and two reflectors, and the antenna's beams go from the reflector across the radiator. And these radiators have to be in a horizontal position when they're mounted; otherwise, there is another way of mounting is when the antenna pole joints are vertical. The best position for the radiators is when they are in a horizontal position; that's when they can establish the best communication because they radiate the best.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Blagojevic, you are looking at the image and the position of the radiators. Can you tell us whether at that time, can you remember, when was the position of those radiators just the same on the antenna system on Veliki Zep and other features? Can you remember that and can you confirm the position of the radiators at that time?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: All the operators, as well as the communications officers, know that that's the rule for the antenna to be mounted; that is, radiators have to be in a horizontal position. That's according to our rules and that's how things were done after all.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I will no longer need this schematic. Can you please tell us something about the power that RRU-800 devices used at the time?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: If I tell you that while I was a student at the military academy that already then RRU-800 was a museum exhibit and was discontinued, was no longer produced, then you can imagine too what was the condition of those devices 20 years later, 25 years later. These devices had to use a much reduced power on shorter distances. The full power was 10 watts and reduced power was 5 watts. However, because of the state of repair of these devices, you have to count with a 25 to 30 per cent less power. And why did we reduce the power? It is part of the instructions which says that this is part of a measure of electronic protection and less possibility of interception on the part of the enemy side and conditions with the energy supply because the device had to be supplied either through a generator or through a power network. RR distances were up to 15 kilometres, even up to the Rogatica Brigade, the 2nd Rogatica Brigade, and especially to the Zvornik Brigade, Vlasenica, Veliki Zep, Cer, Gucova, Zvornik. All of that was up to 15 kilometres' distance. I wouldn't be able to give you the precise distances. I would have to take measurements, but I don't have a map in front of me, so it's difficult for me to tell you exactly. At that time, I had a map and I knew exactly what the distances were.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me something about the meaning of the so-called duplex connection. We have come across this, but we need you to explain the term for us.

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Let me explain. A duplex connection is speech on one frequency and reception on another frequency. A duplex connection can only be established with radio relay devices, and radio-sets can only establish a simplex connection. It takes a radio relay device to be able to establish a duplex connection.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Does this mean that if you have a couple of RRU-800 devices, a conversation can only take place on two different frequencies between one point and another?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, correctly, and that's what was always planned. Two frequencies were always taken into account when planning communication.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: How were the frequencies determined for different RRU-800 routes?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Frequencies for RRU-800 were determined based on the technical characteristics of each particular device. A minimum difference between the emission and reception frequencies had to be at least 50 kilohertz, and that was what determined the frequency. I, as the chief of communications of the Drina Corps in this particular case, was not the one who determined frequencies. The frequencies, some of them at least, were determined by the Main Staff, the chief of communications for the Main Staff; and some were adjusted to the characteristics of the hubs in Cer, Gucevo, Strazbenica, and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know who specifically designated these frequencies for RRU-800 communications between the command of the Drina Corps in Vlasenica and Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: From Vlasenica to Veliki Zep, the frequencies were determined by the chief of communications of the Main Staff because that's communications between the Main Staff and the corps command, but it was the same route for communications towards units. Veliki Zep is also a hub for the command of the Drina Corps. From Veliki Zep to Cer, that was within the jurisdiction of the communications authorities of another state, and from Cer to Gucevo as well. From Gucevo to Zvornik, the relay communications were adjusted, but it was decided in principle by the chief of communications who was in charge of that territory. Neither I nor the chief of communications of the Main Staff were responsible for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: When you mentioned another state, did you mean Yugoslavia as it was then?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Now, could we look at another attachment from the findings of Mr. Rodic, 1D322, page 13 and page 14. In your bundle, it's the second tab, also pages 13 and 14.

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: You said page 13?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: This document was shown to our expert, Rodic, but I see that it is not translated in English. There are just few locations and references, number of references.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you please tell me -- or rather, can you confirm if this is the plan of frequencies -- or, in fact, you tell me yourself what is this.

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: As you say, this is the plan of frequencies; however, it contains information about radio relay routes that I submitted to the chief of communications of the Main Staff. You will remember my explanation from a moment ago that we were not in charge of certain hubs, so we couldn't determine frequencies for some of our units. Therefore, I gathered radio relay frequencies from our units and submitted them to our chief of communications to have it on record to avoid messing up.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, in addition to this document where frequencies are marked, do you know if these frequencies had ever been changed during the war?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: These frequencies have not been changed from the beginning of the war because there was no interference. Now, whether anybody listened in, I don't want to go into that. We did our best to avoid listening and interception, but there was no interference and no jamming, so there was no need to change these frequencies.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us if the Drina Corps was even able to change these frequencies. Did you, as chief of communications, or anyone else in the Drina Corps have the ability to change these frequencies?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: I, as chief of communications, did not have the right, the power, to change it because none of these frequencies was specifically the frequency of the Drina Corps, which would have given me jurisdiction. But in this case, I was not able to, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: What about these end radio relay stations in Vlasenica and in Zvornik, were they stationary?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Radio relay stations, when they operate, they're always stationary; that's the law.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Were they integrated with other communications systems?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Radio relay communications, whenever possible, are integrated with both radio and wire communications; however, in our case they were integrated with only wire communications.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: These stations, RRU-800, could they be moved from one location to another?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Radio relay stations were movable; however, unlike radio devices, radio relay stations beam in one direction, so moving them would be like looking for a needle in a haystack. They work point to point; and if you move the station, then the other participant would have to search for that point in the territory.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness repeat the last thing he said about antennas.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you repeat the last thing that interpreters didn't hear. You said the stations were working point to point; and if you move the station, then the other participant has to search for that point in the field. And after that, you said something else; so if you can remember please say it again.

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: A station that would relocate would be moving on a vehicle, therefore. How would we mount the antenna then? The rule did not prescribe that, and it would be impossible anyway. That is why work in motion was not applied. It only operated on a stationary basis.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: You've already said this, I believe, but please confirm. Does this mean that while you were chief of communications, these stations, RRU-800, were not moved from one point to another?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: They were not. They worked on a stationary basis.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I have just one more question for you: Can you tell me, was it at all possible to establish direct radio relay communication with RRU-800 from Vlasenica to Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: In view of the lay of the land, it was impossible to have direct communication between Vlasenica and Zvornik. There was no optic visibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Blagojevic. I have no further questions for you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you so much, Mr. Zivanovic. Mr. Ostojic, you indicated 30 minutes. Yes, Mr. Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. President. I have a few questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, go ahead. Please introduce yourself with the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Blagojevic. My name is Predrag Nikolic, an attorney on the team of the accused Ljubisa Beara. I have a few questions regarding the technical characteristics of the TCE switchboard. Tell me, was it possible, with the system of communications that you explained and that operated in 1995, to establish communications with the public PTT service?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Well, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: How?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Quite simply, from the PTT switchboard in any place where we were, the corps command brought a number of plug-ins from the PTT to us; and in every brigade command, we brought in connections from TC -- from the PTT service to our own communications. We had a link in any case.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Does it mean that from the corps command you could directly to any participant on a PTT line in any location in Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: You could talk with any participant, not only in Republika Srpska but also to Germany, to the US, China, Russia, through PTT lines.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Does that mean that that participant from the PTT network, let's say from Valjevo, was able to call the corps command?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Was he able in the same way to call lower units?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Where were these PTT lines installed at the corps command?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: At the corps command, we connected them to the switchboard that existed in the building of the corps - that's the former administrative building of the mining company, the bauxite processing plant - and there we connected it to our TC 40.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Did I understand this correctly? If a call from a PTT switchboard in any town or place in Yugoslavia comes to the switchboard at the corps command, the operator would be able to connect another collocutor, not only in the corps, but also in lower units?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I have no other questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Nikolic. Madam Nikolic, you intimated you were not going to cross-examine this witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's correct, Your Honour. Thank you. I have no questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. The same applies to you, Mr. Lazarevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Madam Faveau? Mr. Petrusic will be cross-examining the witness instead.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Blagojevic.

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: My name is Nenad Petrusic; and on behalf of the Defence team of General Miletic, I will ask you a few questions. At the outset, I'd like to look into your relationship as chief of communications in the Drina Corps with the command; that is, the staff. You were subordinated, as you said, to the Chief of Staff of the Drina Corps?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: This section of yours, you were part of a section, the arm of communications?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Could you say that again.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Was your organ of communications on the level of section?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: We should have had another five men; however, it was wartime and there was shortage of personnel. I was alone.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: And you had one unit for technical maintenance, conditionally speaking, and that was the 5th Communications Battalion of the Drina Corps; correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: It was a unit for establishing and maintaining communications; whereas, technical maintenance is something entirely different.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Thank you for that clarification. Did you, therefore, as chief of communications, participate in the preparation and submission of proposals to the corps commander or Chief of Staff when certain combat documents were developed, documents that involved the communications organ in a certain operation?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: I participated in the preparation of documents for every operation, precisely for the reasons stated, because personnel and equipment of communications need to be employed and communications need to be planned.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: So you made a proposal to the commander how to organize this communication system?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we call up 5D1182. We have a draft translation for this, and I would like it provided to the Chamber. It has also been supplied to the Prosecution and the Defence teams of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Petrusic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Mr. Blagojevic, do you have a document before you marked 5D1182?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: This is a document from the command of the Drina Corps, dated 14 March 1994, signed by the commander, Major-General Milenko Zivanovic. At the top of the document, we read: "Establishing a section of communications for the requirements of..." please let me read this, "... for the requirements of the Tactical Group 1. Order." Does it say in this order that from the composition of the 5th Communications Battalion, a movable, a mobile, communications section should be set up that would consist of the commander of the section, operator of the radio relay device, an encryptor and Teletypist, and one driver?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: In this order, item 2, do you see that the equipment in this section of communications are to be RRU-1 and KZS? Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: I see it. KZ is a station.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Please let me ask my question, and that was going precisely what you anticipated. This acronym, KZS, is what?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Encrypting station.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: So these items, 1 and 2, was it you or someone from your communications organ that proposed it to the commander? That was within your area of expertise.

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Petrusic, I prepared the whole order, all of the items.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: We see below, in item 5, that the dead-line for executing this task is the 16th of March, 1994. So is it the case that this station at Pribicevac had to be established and put into operation by this dead-line, 16th March?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: In the order, you read that the commander of the tactical group of Pribicevac shall inform the commander at 1200 hours, and that was the dead-line for the order, because with the establishment of radio relay communication, it was possible to inform the commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Was it really put into operation then?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Did it then continue to operate throughout 1994 and even in June 1995?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: From the time when it was established until the completion of Srebrenica operation, this communication worked.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: We heard here that this communication started to operate in January 1995, and it was even given a frequency, 259.275 megahertz. So I want to know is it the case that in January 1995 some other type of communication was established, apart from this?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: This was the only radio relay communication between Veliki Zep and Pribicevac using RRU-1, and 275 megahertz was not possible because the frequency range for this device is 230 to 270 megahertz.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: You probably misheard me. I was talking about a frequency of 259.275 megahertz, so the first one is 259.

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: 259 was possible with -- I don't have the plan of frequencies before me, and I don't know by heart what the frequencies were, but 275 was impossible was -- because of the characteristics of the device.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: But to conclude, it was not established in January 1995?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: No, it was not.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Could we move on to 5D1181. This is also an order from the command of the Drina Corps dated 11 December 1994 issued by Major-General Milenko Zivanovic, commander of the Drina Corps. And it's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Petrusic, I'm sorry to interrupt you. But if you look at page 28, line 16, when you are describing this document, you say an order from command of the Drina Corps, dated 11th December 1994, issued by Major-General Milenko Zivanovic. It is, indeed, issued by Milenko Zivanovic, but the date we have here is 1st February 1994. So is it --

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No. But I want to make sure that the translation that we have --

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, Your Honours. You will -- I read this date as the 11th of December. But it's also possible it could be the 11th of February, because in the copy that I have in the Serbian language, yes, it's really possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. But --

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mrs. Faveau has just drawn my attention --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: -- I want you to think further about your answer. Could you please go to the last line of that document, which starts with: [B/C/S spoken]. There you have the date again: "Dead-line for the execution is." Then you have a date which looks as if it is 10th February 1994. Anyway, let's say you will look into this later on. I don't think it is important for the time being. Let's not waste or lose time on this, but please look into it so that if there is a -- and there in the English translation we will correct it. Yes, Madam Faveau.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We will probably take a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, no. We don't need a break. We can continue with the question unless it's referred -- oh, it's break time. Yes, Madam Faveau.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would just like to clarify one point. This is an unofficial translation done by the Defence, so the date wasn't quite clear. And when my team translated this document, the date is the 1st of February, 1994. In fact, they referred to this last sentence of the document. This is why we have the date of the 1st of February, 1994, because the date was not very legible in the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Anyway, you think about this. We'll have a 25-minute break starting from now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. So, irrespective of the correct date of this document, which I think should be February and not December, let's proceed with your question, please, to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. During the break, we had consultations. It was probably the month of February. Actually, it was the 1st of February, 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Mr. Blagojevic, could you please look at the document 5D1181, and you will see. Do you have that document in front of you?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: The commander of the Drina Corps orders that a radio interception group force should be established in order to detect and monitor enemy communication in the area of electronic surveillance, and then he provides the location which is Jeceva, Zebanjsko, Ljeskovik, Kamenica, and Zepa. Do you know that this radio eavesdropping group was, indeed, established; or rather, did you, as the chief of communications, or the 5th Engineering Battalion participate in the equipping of this particular radio eavesdropping group?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: I was aware of this order. You made a slip of the tongue. It was not the 5th Engineering Battalion, but the 5th Communication Battalion. We were informed and aware of this order because information was to be transferred from a hill Sarampov, (Pribicevac), to the corps command and the organs that had use of the information that was transmitted, and that's what we did.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: It may be concluded from this order that what should be monitored were radio communication between Srebrenica and Zepa. Was that something that was within the purview of the intelligence organs, and I'm talking about the collection of information here?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Precisely so. The radio eavesdropping group was established in order to listen in to the enemy radio communication in the territories of Zepa and Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: In the corps command, did you have another similar group; or to be more precise, are you aware of the existence of 4th Radio Reconnoitring or Reconnaissance group within that corps?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: The radio reconnaissance platoon existed within the Drina Corps, and it was headquartered in Vlasenica. But most of the men were at forward points or posts as radio eavesdropping groups, and there were other such eavesdropping group. And if you want me to, I can --

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Their main task was to collect and monitor radio traffic in the enemy territory. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: And the information collected in this way was then submitted to the command organs?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: You also spoke already about that, but now I'm asking you again what was the main aspect of communication lines between the Drina Corps and the brigade commands?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Between the Drina Corps and the brigade commands, the main line of communication was a radio relay communication line.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: It seems that you've already told us that there was also a wire connection; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: A wire connection existed from the beginning to the very end with the Milica Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: When it comes to the switchboard, more specifically at the corps command, did a civilian number came there?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I've already said that to Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Yes. I'm just using this for the basis for my further questions. This civilian number, was it further on distributed through extension numbers to the offices of certain officers?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: The commander and the Chief of Staff, the chief of security, and the chief of intelligence had direct civilian numbers. And there was one civilian number that was attached to the switchboard, and that one number had extensions to other members of the command from the switchboard.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: And, now, what was the civilian treatment of this postal communication between the brigade command and the battalion command?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: The brigade command and the battalion commands were not very often connected because of the possibilities and the positions that were held by the battalion commands. Wherever it was possible, it was used but that was not very often.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now have document 1D338, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: While this is being brought up into e-court, I would kindly ask you to confirm that this is the system of radio relay lines of which we -- you spoke at great length when answering Mr. Zivanovic's questions, the schematic image.

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. This is a schematic that I did myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Mr. Blagojevic, from the Main Staff to Vlasenica, i.e., the Drina Corps, was the radio relay line protected? Was it safe?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] From the Main Staff --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, one moment, one moment. Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. It's unclear as to when this particular schematic was drawn and to what period of time my colleague is referring to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Could you address that, Mr. Petrusic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Mr. Blagojevic, this schematic that you have in front of you, was it in force in 1995, more specifically in July 1995?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Can you now answer my previous question, which was as --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think we have to. Mr. Vanderpuye [sic], you have addressed to the witness a question which does not really answer the points raised by Mr. Vanderpuye. Mr. Vanderpuye, yes. Mr. Vanderpuye would like to know, before Mr. Blagojevic answers your previous question, when this schematic, this particular schematic was drawn and to what period of time you are referring to. So your question suggested to the witness that the schematic that he has in front of you, without indicating when it was drawn and to which period when it was drawn, you are asking him whether it was in force in 1995, more specifically in July 1995. But when was it drawn? When was this schematic drawn, before or after July 1995; and who is the author of it?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Mr. Blagojevic, you heard the President's suggestion. Do you want me to repeat the question at all?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: You don't have to. This schematic was drawn when the corps was established, which means in November 1992, and I'm the author. It was attached to the orders that applied to the communications, and you can see that in the heading there is a title "Attachment 2."

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: As you have already told us, this communications system was applied in July 1995?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: And let's go back to my previous question. We're talking about the Main Staff and Vlasenica or the command of the Drina Corps. Was the radio relay line between the two protected? Was it safe?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: From the Main Staff to the corps command, as well as to the other corps command --

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Mr. Blagojevic, hold on. I'm only interested in this particular route: The Main Staff-Vlasenica.

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: The Main Staff-Vlasenica was 0574 radio relay route, as you can see it on the schematic. FM 200 was the marking of the device, and that route was fully protected which means both written and oral communication was -- were protected. There was a total of eight channels that were all safe.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: In order to establish a communication with Zvornik, you had to go via Veliki Zep-Cer-Gucevo-Zvornik. Did I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: This particular radio relay route, was it protected along its entire length or just in some of its parts?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: The radio relay line between Vlasenica and Zvornik was protected and safe, and it was impossible to listen in between Veliki Zep in Cer. And as for Vlasenica-Veliki Zep, Cer-Gucevo, and Gucevo-Zvornik, this is where it was possible to listen in under the condition that you enter the radio relay beam which was difficult because we applied measures of anti-electronic protection. You could only intercept oral communication, which was impossible with the written communication because the written communication was always encrypted, and that's how they were broadcast.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Petrusic, as a layman of communication and without having the translation, it's almost impossible to follow. For example, I couldn't locate in this schematic where the Main Staff is, and I couldn't find the 0574 radio route either. So could you bear that in mind?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Mr. Blagojevic, kindly look at the schematic that is in front of you and follow the markings on it -- let me rephrase that. In the schematic that you have in front of you, the marking Crna Rijeka, does it imply the Main Staff?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Crna Rijeka stands for the Main Staff, and this is what you can see written above the circle, the GSV of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: It is left to the centre --

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Left to Veliki Zep --

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Hold on. It is left to the central square marked as Veliki Zep?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Kindly bear in mind that these documents will be returned to us. Could you please make a circle around that particular location.

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: I'm referring to the location of Crna Rijeka or the Main Staff that we have just identified there. And could you please also answer my next question -- or, actually, it was the second question by the Presiding Judge, which is the radio relay route 0674, is that the radio relay route that went from the location marked as Vlasenica to the Veliki Zep square?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Petrusic, now I found 0674. It was formerly translated as 0574, so that's the reason I couldn't find it. Let's move. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour, for your intervention. I believe that now this problem has been removed, and we have now identified the position of the Main Staff. And now I would like to call up document 5D1186 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- 1186.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, while we load this document. Mr. Vanderpuye, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Actually, I'm not convinced that we have resolved the issue as you might be. The translation was 0574, and it was mentioned in connection with the corps command and Main Staff. 0674 traverses the corps command and Veliki Zep, which is the relay point, and I'm not sure that that's what the witness was referring to, at least it's not clear to me in the record. So if my learned friend would clarify that issue, I think that would make the record clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Petrusic, who is quite familiar with this schematic, or you on cross-examination. I suggest that Mr. Petrusic tries to sort this out now.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Mr. Blagojevic, could you please answer this objection. When it comes to the connection between the Main Staff and Vlasenica, what was Veliki Zep in that connection? Let's deal with that. Was Veliki Zep the radio relay hub for all lines irrespective of their origin?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Veliki Zep was a radio relay you hub. It was the hub of the Main Staff, and in this case of the Drina Corps as well. From the relay devices at Veliki Zep to the command of the Main Staff, there was a multi-wire cable.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know if my learned friend is happy with this explanation; but in any case, he will have an opportunity to cross-examine the witness and ask for further clarification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Let's proceed. I saw Mr. Vanderpuye nodding.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Mr. Blagojevic, was Veliki Zep connected with cables, to put it in lay terms, with the Main Staff?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, by cables or by a wire connection.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And now I would like to call 5D1186 up in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Mr. Blagojevic, before you, you have a document which is entitled: "The overview of the secret codes of the corps command." Would you please tell us whether this overview of the secret codes refers to the Drina Corps and its secret codes?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Who was it who assigned those codes -- no, I withdraw that. What period of time is it that these codes were applied?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: This overview of codes applies from the moment when the Drina Corps was established. Sometime in 1994 the codes were changed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: How often did the codes change?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Sometimes two times annually. And in this particular case, these were applied for two years; and then there was a strong suspicion that the conversations may have been listened in and then codes changed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: And when the codes changed in your superior command, in the Main Staff, or in any other commands or any other corps, you would I suppose be informed about the change?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: I should have been informed; however, the chief of communications of the Main Staff was not duty-bound to inform us. He could have done it without us being in the know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Who was it who changed the codes, was it the superior command?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: The codes are changed and then communicated to step further. So it is the Main Staff for the corps and brigade commands, and the corps for the battalion commands.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: In the fourth column, we have a marking "TGR." What does this stand for?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: TGR stands for telegraphy.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: These are codes for teleprinter stations or Teletype stations of particular units of the Drina Corps?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. You can see the Drina Corps units starting with 22 and further on, and those units had Teletyping machines.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Now, these secret codes, do they refer exclusively to the units of the Drina Corps and not to the places that are part of those units' names?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: These codes refer only to the units, nothing else.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And, finally, we have another document, 5D187 -- 5D1187.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: We have a list of numbers to identify commanding officers of the Drina Corps here. Please, can you explain what this schematic means, what this list of number means.

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: This list of numbers to identify commanding officers is attached to the list of secret codes; and when somebody asks for code Zlatar 412, that means he's looking for the corps commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: And this column from 1 to 10, what does it mean?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: That means from the 1st till the 10th of the month, from the 11th to the 20th of the month, to identify the commander, you use the number 657; from the 21st to the 31st of the month, the commander's number is 150.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: These identification numbers for COs, are they changed every month?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: This list of identification numbers is subject to change, just as the list of codes; if they are revealed, divulged, they have to be changed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Mr. Blagojevic, I have no further questions for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the end of my examination, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Petrusic. The Gvero Defence team and the Pandurevic Defence team have indicated they don't wish to cross-examine this witness. I see a confirmation of that. So it's you, Mr. Vanderpuye, now. Are you going to stick to your one hour?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I'm hoping to, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So are we, Mr. Vanderpuye. L. Et's proceed, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Blagojevic.

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: My name is Mr. Vanderpuye. I'm going to put some questions to you on behalf of the Prosecution in relation to your direct examination. I'll try to be as brief as I can, but you did cover a lot of ground on your direct, and so let's see how you get through this. You indicated, just initially, that the RRU-800 covers a frequency range from 600 to 900 megahertz. Do you recall that testimony, sir?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And, in fact, in the frequency plan that you were referred to by my colleague Mr. Zivanovic, there is a frequency that is indicated in that plan that runs from Vlasenica to Veliki Zep of 922 megahertz, which by your testimony would be outside of the possible range of communication for that device.

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: That's a mistake, a typing mistake.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Whose typing mistake? I think we need to be clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You say that's a typing mistake, Mr. Blagojevic?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Let me suggest to you that that document is actually handwritten and that frequency is handwritten, as you've testified to, by you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: If I could just have in e-court, so that I can show Mr. Blagojevic what I'm talking about, 65 ter 2823. All right. If we could just page down a little bit, I think right in the middle of the screen, you can see where it says "922/680."

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I don't know if you have that in front of you now, Mr. Blagojevic, but I would refer you to number 2 that's indicated on the document you should have in front of, you which is indicated by an ERN number ending in 791. You can see where it's written in. It's handwritten 922/680, 6-8-0. That's a radio relay route 0607. You see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, here it is. I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And you say that that's a mistake?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: A mistake.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Actually, sir, the mistake is that the RRU-800 has a frequency range or capacity from 610 megahertz to 960 megahertz. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Possibly.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You're not sure?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: I'm no longer sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Now, in 1995, you were the chief of communications for the Drina Corps, right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: He has already answered that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And you were responsible for maintaining all communications within that system, within the corps system?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Right, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And that involved maintaining communications with all the battalions, all the brigades, and the Main Staff?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And you said before that you were intimately involved in the planning stage of any giving operation that was undertaken by the corps?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: So you had to know the number of units that would participate in any given operation?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You had to know where they were positioned and where they were going?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You had to know the locations of their command posts and who their commanders were?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And you had to assist in planning an operation to make sure that you could provide adequate operational communications among those units?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And in determining what appropriate equipment that you would use, you had to consider also the type of equipment that was available to you?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You had to consider the terrain on which that equipment was going to be used?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You had to consider the distance over which that equipment had to be used, whether it's radio relay, radio, wire, telegraph, or telegram?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And you also had to pay attention to security issues to make sure that those communications were safe and protected from the enemy?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Now, over your career, you've participated in the planning of a number of operations; that's fair to say, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You participated in the communications plan that was developed for Krivaja 95?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Probably. I can't remember now which operation it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. You participated in developing the communications plan that was used in the Srebrenica operation?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And that was in 1995, July, right?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: In July, right.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You participated in preparing the communications plan for a subsequent operation, Operation Stit, 1995, in November?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: In November 1995, I don't know what operation it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Well, we'll get back to that in just a minute. You also participated in an operation in 1993 by the name of Operation Proboj, right?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't know which operation it was; the name of the operation itself doesn't help.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: But it was an operation that began on the 24th November 1992 and ended 3rd February 1993; you remember that?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: If that's the operation from axis towards Srebrenica, then I do remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: This was an operation that involved the liberation of the Podrinje region, and it was designed to force the enemy into a small area to create the conditions for the subsequent operation which was carried out in 1995. Does that help refresh your recollection?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: That's right. That's the operation I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And in relation to that operation, there were combat activities that were carried out in Kamenica, Cerska, Konjevic Polje, Bratunac, Visegrad, and Rogatica, right?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: In that operation, there was fighting in Konjevic Polje, Cerska, and Kamenica; whereas, Rogatica and Visegrad are on another side. It's not the same operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
