utterances.text: All right. And with respect to your participation in that operation, you were assigned to coordinate the actions for it along with Mile Kosoric and Captain Radenko Visnjic. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: I don't recall that I made it with the two of them, but if you --

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: If I could just have 65 ter 3413, so that the witness can briefly take a look at it.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. If I could just direct your attention to the bottom of your screen, I think you can see your name in there, where it's indicated the members of the group for the coordination of the actions -- of actions are: Miladin Prstojevic, Mile Kosoric, and you, Nedo Blagojevic. Can you see that there?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And that's accurate, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: It must be true because it's an order from the corps command, but I participated in so many of these operations that I can't recall everything.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. But you do recall that you were tasked with setting up communications in relation to the carrying out of this particular operation?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: I remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. And, in particular, you were tasked with setting up or coordinating those communications among the units that were involved in the operation and their commanders?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. And you also had to set up communications with the Yugoslav Army as well, right, the Uzice Corps?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: I don't recall that; but, generally speaking, our corps command and the command of the Uzice Corps were able to communicate.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Now, the units that participated in that operation included the Zvornik Brigade, 1st Light Infantry Zvornik Brigade, Bratunac Brigade; it also included elements outside the Drina Corps, including the 1st Krajina Corps and the 2nd Krajina Corps, as well as the 65th Motorised Protection Regiment of the Main Staff, right?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: There was some interruption in the line. In that operation, the Zvornik Brigade was involved, the Bircani Brigade, there was one battalion from the 1st Krajina Corps, the Bratunac Brigade, the Milic Brigade, and the Independent Battalion of Skelani. Those are the units I know about.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Right. And I take it you know who Vinko Pandurevic is?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Vinko Pandurevic was the commander of the Zvornik Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And what was his role in the operation in which you participated in 1993, 1992 November to February 1993, that we've been discussing?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: He commanded the Zvornik Brigade, and they were advancing from Zvornik via Kamenica, Konjevic Polje -- I cannot remember the exact axis at this moment, but it was certainly via Kamenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Thank you for that. Now, if I've understood your testimony correctly with respect to radio intercepts, you're not suggesting, sir, that the VRS was not being intercepted by the Bosnian army, are you?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I recall, the witness didn't say this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Vanderpuye --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: If we can see the reference page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: In any case, it's cross-examination, so let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Are you suggesting that the Bosnian army was unable to intercept VRS radio relay communications, Mr. Blagojevic? Is that what the point of your testimony is?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: If your question relates to radio communication from November 1992 to March 1993, they were able to -- I mean, the enemy was able to intercept our radio communications, if that was the point of your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: If I could just have just one moment. Could I have 65 ter 3425.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I don't know if you have the document in front of you now, but I'll refer you to this document which is dated 22nd April 1993. This is a document that is authored by or signed by Drago Nikolic, as the chief of security of the Zvornik Brigade, and it's a document that was transmitted through the channels of the intelligence organ. In the first paragraph of that document, it says: "We have confirmation that the enemy is intensively intercepting our radio and radio relay communications. Particularly active are the interception centres in Tuzla and at Dvor." Now, that would be after March 1993 that you've indicated that they lost the ability to intercept your communications.

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: I don't know what you have been following; but in terms of radio communications, I said that in 1995 I placed KZU devices, not 1993, because in 1993, I did not have KZU devices; whereas, in 1995, in June, I mounted KZU devices for the oncoming operation. That's when they were not able to listen in; however, in the period you are talking about, they were able to listen and intercept.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. So it's accurate to say that in 1993, when this document was authored, that the Bosnian army had the ability to intercept VRS radio relay communications?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Radio communications were easier to intercept. Radio relay communications were harder, sometimes impossible, to intercept.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I appreciate the clarification, but my question is: As the document states, is it the case that the Bosnian army had the ability to intercept radio relay communications? You'll see that written in paragraph -- in the first paragraph of this document authored by Mr. Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: I can see that and I agree, and that's what I told you. Radio communications, yes; radio relay harder, some radio relay impossible.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. If you read further on in this document, Mr. Nikolic explains what the nature of this problem is. And in part, he says that even the most responsible commanding officers in the units are prone to negligence; and then he proposes a number of things that should be changed in order to accommodate the problem, such as prevent unnecessarily long conversations, prohibit the use of Motorola hand-sets, and change the frequencies in call-signs more often. You were aware of that in 1993, weren't you, Mr. Blagojevic?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: I was aware of that even earlier. Even in December 1992, I wrote an order that was signed by the corps commander to the effect that all actions related to combat activities should be related only in writing. It was sent from the corps to brigades. Precisely for these reasons, it was said that conversations by radio should be minimised.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. You said it wasn't until June 1995 that you actually got what you've called KZ crypto protection for communications. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: KZU 63 for radio protection, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Would it surprise you to learn that the Bosnian army was actually aware of your request to have those devices installed?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: If I could have 65 ter 3407 in e-court for the witness to take a look at.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: What you should have in front of you is a report from the 2nd Corps command directed towards their intelligence organ, which indicates that you specifically requested, demanded, the installation of KZU 31 cryptographic data equipment to be installed. In part, this is based on the fact that they say that you were able to break a code of theirs. Does this suggest to you, sir, that as late as July 1995, they were actually picking up your radio communications, communications that you were having with respect to the protection of your radio -- your radio relay system?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: As for the report of the intelligence organ of the BiH army, it speaks about the KZU 31, which was already there. It must be a mistake there.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter is not sure whether the witness said that it does speak or does not speak.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Because from 1993 in March, there was a TG 40 or 41 device on Pribicevac for the encryption of written information. In 1994, this encrypting device was replaced by the KZU 31. So that this is a mistake. That's the only thing I can say, but a hundred per cent.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You do admit, though, that you made a specific request for KZU protection in or around June of 1995, right?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: What is referred to in here, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Maybe I requested a KZU 61 for speech protection.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. Let me refer you to 65 ter 3412. What you should have in front of you is a request signed by General Mladic to fix certain radio relay routes involving -- involving the KZU 61 device. In particular, he talks about a radio relay route from Veliki Zep to Cer that had been fixed, and he also indicates that he's requesting the same team to come and fix other problems in the radio relay communications network. And he says: "Until now, we used the radio device for protecting speech KZU 61." He says: "Due to the decreased use and the quality and convergence path, we are unable to use the speech protection device KZU 61." In other words, those lines of communication were not protected. Now, you can see that was the state of affairs in 1993, right?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: This is probably a mistake. It must have referred to KZU 71 because KZU 61 protects just one path, one line; whereas, KZU 71 protects a group which contains eight paths or eight lines.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Well, could it be that the KZU 61 that is protecting a particular path relates to the use of the SMC device?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: As for the SMC device, it could not have been 61 because the SMC had 120 channels, and we had -- we did not have an encryption protection. It was only because of its higher frequency that an SMC was more difficult to listen in to.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. The 120-channel radio relay communication between Veliki Zep and Cer is an SMC communication, right?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's the whole point.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And that operated between 4 and 5 gigahertz, you said?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And in July 1995, there was also a back-up RRU-800 communications path between Veliki Zep and Cer, right?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: There was a reserve option even in 1993, but this path was repaired and returned into good working order.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: When was it repaired --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, one moment. Madam Faveau.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I didn't want to interrupt before because I didn't know what the Prosecutor was getting at, but it seems to me that this document has nothing to do with the Drina Corps. Perhaps the Prosecutor could tell us what the connection is, because the 1st and 2nd Corps are the only corps mentioned in this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Vanderpuye, if you could answer that, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Yes. It might be that my colleague perhaps has missed the issue. The document specifically talks about the radio relay direction from Veliki Zep to Cer, which is integral to this witness's testimony concerning the Drina Corps radio relay path between Vlasenica and Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Madam Faveau.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. But could we perhaps read paragraph 2 in its entirety because the document has mentioned this direction, but it also mention which line is not being used. It talks about Kozara-Banja Luka and the equipment designed to protect voice KZU 61 for the 1st and 2nd Krajina Corps. I know nothing about these technicalities. Perhaps the witness could explain this to us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Vanderpuye. Do you wish to comment on that?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I'm sure she can put it to the witness if she wants to. The point of the issue is that this document describes that the condition of that line between Veliki Zep and Cer was in disrepair at a certain point, that it was fixed, that it's 120-channel radio relay device which is the same device that was, in fact, in 1995 on the same line --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. Blagojevic, do you need to hear the question again or can you answer it?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: My question was, if I recall: When was it fixed?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Your question is on page 51 between lines 23 and line 1 on page 52.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Since I was in Vlasenica, and this was within the purview of the Chief of Staff -- chief of communications of the Main Staff, it must have lasted for two or three, days but our lines of communication were not interrupted. As you've told it yourself, RRU-800 was in reserve, and I suppose that that's when the SMC was replaced by the RRU-800 in order to have the lines of communication working. Then upon the repairs were completed, the whole thing was reinstated.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. And so my question is: When was it repaired, if you recall?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. Do you know whether or not that system, that is, the SMC line between Veliki Zep and Cer, went down at any point between July or June or August of 1995?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: There were no problems in 1995 with that path during the bombardment.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: What about in August of 1995, do you recall if there were any problems at that point?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, there were no problems.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: One of the people that is mentioned in this document, 65 ter 3412, is an individual by the name of Major Djuro Rodic, engineer. Do you see that name in front of you?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: He testified in this case in August -- he testified actually on the 24th of May and on the 12th of June 2007. He said that in August of 1995, he was asked by Mr. Zivanovic: "While you were there, did you service that line? I think you mentioned that a couple of times." And he says: "Preliminarily, we fixed those 120-channel paths because they were the most important ones and then also the 24-channel ones were the RRU-800 ." Why would he be fixing them in August of 1995 if they weren't down?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: It is asked -- Mr. Vanderpuye called the witness to speculate about this information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: He knows the answer to that question or he doesn't. I mean, we don't go on speculation from Mr. Blagojevic. Now, I think he's qualified enough to answer this question. Yes, Mr. Blagojevic --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm qualified enough.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. And can you answer the question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm qualified enough, but this was not within my purview. What mattered to me was that I had an uninterrupted line of communication with the units. I was never informed about that line being down because the person in charge was the chief of communications of the Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Well, had the line been down, then the back-up RRU-800 device would go into service; is that fair?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And in order for you to make use --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: It is misstatement of testimony of Mr. Rodic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: How about this, how about this. Maybe this will satisfy you. How about page 12120, line 15 to 18; maybe that will help you out a little bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: He has never told that such that the lines were interrupted --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. But I suggest that you look at the reference that Mr. Vanderpuye has just mentioned. Now if you need time to look at it, I will give you time to look at it; otherwise, we will proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: If it's part of his testimony, but he didn't say that the line was interrupted.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: The quote from that transcript is: "And while you were there, did you service that line?" That's the question, actually. "I think you mentioned that a couple of times. "A. Preliminarily, we fixed those 120-channel paths because they were the most important ones and then also the 24-channel ones with the RRU-800."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Vanderpuye -- Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: He said that they do the service, but not because the line was interrupted. It is a point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Let's carry on. Mr. Vanderpuye, please --

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Let me ask one other thing if I could, Mr. President. Maybe this will clarify.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: It continues, and says: "Okay. How long were you at the facility in August 1995 fixing those parts?" And the answer is: "I think we completed that in two days." I think that makes it pretty clear that some fixing going on of the lines that was witness testified about, and that's what was put to this witness, just so the record is clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Witness, from your knowledge and recollection, what's your answer to that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I just now remembered. In the month of August, I was not in the command post in Vlasenica; I was in another location and performing other duties as well. So I really can't answer this question because I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Well, you were the chief of communications for the Drina Corps, and that particular radio relay route was integral to your ability to communicate with your subordinate units, right?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And if there was a problem getting a communication through on that line, that's something that you needed to know about as the chief of communications; otherwise, you wouldn't be able to advise the Chief of Staff or the commander as to what to do in a given situation?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: I've just told you that. In the month of August and September, I was not in Vlasenica. Major Jerdjevic was standing in for me, and I can't answer your question because I wasn't there. I wasn't abreast of the situation. I performed other tasks elsewhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. I just wanted to draw your attention to 65 ter 2823, and that's the frequency plan that my colleague went over with you. This is the plan that I think you indicated that you, yourself, prepared.

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. And you say that you prepared it so that there would be a record of the frequencies that were actually in use; is that right?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: That is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You also said that those frequencies never changed from the beginning of the war; is that right?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: True, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Now, if the frequencies hadn't changed at the beginning of the war in 1992, what was the special reason to document these frequencies in 1993?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: In order to update data and plan -- and possible planning of other radio relay lines in order to avoid any confusion or a mix-up.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Well, all that information would have already existed, wouldn't it, as of 1992. So what was the special reason that you had in October of 1993 to document frequencies that already existed within the structure -- within the communication structure?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Most probably, there was a request on the part of the chief of communications of the Main Staff; probably he requested information about the existing lines.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Now, with respect to the particular radio relay route from Vlasenica to Zvornik, that involved going from Vlasenica to Veliki Zep, then from Veliki Zep to Cer, then from Cer to Gucevo, and then from Gucevo to Zvornik. That's correct, right?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Now, with respect to those particular radio relay paths, your plan here establishes that there was a frequency between Vlasenica and Veliki Zep of 922 megahertz and 680 megahertz. You see that there under number 2, right?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And you can also see that there is a frequency indicated for the command of the Zvornik Light Infantry Brigade to Gucevo, and it says radio relay route 65. That's under number 4 --

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: -- and that indicates a frequency of 880, it looks like, and 810 megahertz?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Now, between Veliki Zep and Cer, you've indicated nothing with respect to the RRU-800 device - back-up device, I should say - that operates or could operate between those two points. That frequency is not in your documentation?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: This is the confirmation of what I've just said. The chief of communications of the Main Staff asked me to provide information about our end radio relay stations to the hub, and our Main Staff already had information about the frequencies between the hubs and Veliki Zep.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Your plan also doesn't indicate any frequency operating between Gucevo and Cer?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: This frequency plan refers to what the chief of communications of the Main Staff was supposed to update. When I was answering counsel Zivanovic's questions, I mentioned that when there were interruptions, the operators could change the frequency, but they were duty-bound to inform and update everybody concerned. They could do that in case they suspected interference or that they were being listened in.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. But in 1995, you had pretty good information that you were being listened in, right?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: But you have no recollection that there was any change to the frequencies that are indicated in your 1993 plan, right?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: There were no changes because they were not needed. What you asked me about KZU 31 is not correct. KZU 61 that General Mladic signed, again not correct. The radio relay lines and pathways and written information could not have been broken into. Only speech, only oral communication, could have been intercepted.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: If I could maybe just quickly get through this one document; and then we can, with the Court's permission or instruction, maybe take a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I have 65 ter 1150, if we could not broadcast this. That will be 1150A for the benefit of the Court, for the English. He has, I think, B. He should have that in front of him.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] B.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: What I'm showing you, sir, is a radio intercept, and it's indicated that it was taken on the 13th of July, 1995, at 2035 hours, at a frequency of 785 megahertz, which you know corresponds with the frequency range of an RRU-800 device, a radio relay device. And it says in part: "General, sir, is that you? "Yes." One speaker says again: "It's Major Obrenovic. "Greetings." Then it goes on and talks about ambushes that he's been setting up on the wide road and part of Glodjansko Brdo. He says: "He just called me two minutes ago. There's a large column of Turks, three continuous kilometres long, from the school in Glodi. Then he says -- the general says: "Wait. Listen, you can't talk like that on the phone. Call Mane, gather everybody, and send them up there right away." And he answers, in question: "Mane? "Yes." There is evidence in this case that these events as they are related in this intercept transpired as they are written in the intercept. Does that suggest to you that, perhaps, the Bosnian army was, in fact, able to intercept RRU-800 communications along the Vlasenica-Zvornik radio relay path?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: The Vlasenica-Zvornik radio relay path could not be intercepted even by the USA army because that radio relay path did not exist.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Well, it went through a series of connections: One, from Vlasenica to Veliki Zep; two, from Veliki Zep to Cer; three, from Cer to Gucevo; and, four, from Gucevo to Zvornik. Right?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: But when you said radio relay path, that's the way I understood.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. Okay. What I mean is the route, then. Does that intercept and the fact that there is evidence to corroborate it --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Sorry, sorry. But this document clearly reads that it is direction Zvornik-Vlasenica. It doesn't mean any other direction, just Zvornik-Vlasenica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: It is question put to the witness; it is document put to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: What the document says is: "Intercepting the 'Zvornik-Vlasenica' radio relay route." It doesn't say anything about a direct connection or an indirect connection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, go ahead. Go ahead, Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Sir, it's clear, from the fact that this intercept was captured at 785 megahertz, that that implicates that it was captured within the frequency range of an RRU-800 device?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: This is the frequency range of an RRU-800, I agree with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: The Obrenovic that's referred to in this particular intercept is a person that's likely to have been found within that radio relay route, particularly in the Zvornik area, right?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Obrenovic was in the area of Zvornik. Whether this was the exact frequency, I wouldn't know off the cuff. I would have to check. However, I, personally, believe that they couldn't hear Obrenovic, those who were intercepting. They could only hear from the direction of Gucevo. They could hear the general - what general, I wouldn't know - because of the duplex connection.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: A duplex connection has to go through a switchboard, right, Mr. Blagojevic?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: But of course, via a switchboard, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: That's right. And at the point that those connections hit the switchboard, it's possible to hear both collocutors, right, Mr. Blagojevic?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, on a condition that there was an insider who was part of their ranks, who was among their ranks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Any time when it is convenient for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I have only two more questions before the break, if I may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Okay. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You don't know what the frequency was that operated between Cer and Gucevo? You don't know, you don't recall that today, do you?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Look, I don't remember now, unless I look at the plan of frequencies. I don't remember the other frequency other.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And that's -- neither one of them is on your plan, right?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: I don't know, unless I have a plan in front of me.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Well, your plan is in front of you, isn't it, your 1993 plan?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Just a moment.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [via Videolink] Could you give us the 65 ter number?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Yes, it's 65 ter 2823.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Zvornik, according to this plan in front of me, that's not the frequency; not the transmission frequency is correct or the reception frequency.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Tell me what the frequency is, Mr. Blagojevic, between Cer and Gucevo. Let us know when you find it.

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Between Cer and Gucevo?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: I don't have those frequencies. I have Gucevo-Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I think we can take the break at this point, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Vanderpuye. We'll have a 25-minute break now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. Blagojevic, I have here a map that I'm going to try to show you. Let me just get the number for you. That's 65 ter number 3424. I don't know how well you can see that from where you -- you don't see it? Oh, great, okay. I'm not sure how well you can see this map.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: If we can go to the top right-hand corner of that map. All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. Blagojevic, can you read what's on the top right-hand corner of that document?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: "Military secret, strictly confidential, Stit 95."

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: If we could pan down to the lower right-hand of that document as well. That's great.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. Blagojevic, can you read what's at the bottom right-hand corner of this document.

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: "Chief of communications, Lieutenant-Colonel Nedo Blagojevic."

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. And that's you, right?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Now, if we could just move more towards the middle of the map and up. Okay. If we could centre where that flag is at the bottom of the screen, the other direction. Could you move the flag to the middle of the monitor if that's possible. That would be the other way, to the left, yeah. And if we could move downward -- the other way, I'm sorry, up.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. The straight lines that are visible on this map that converge at or near that flag, do those represent the radio relay routes that you've been discussing.

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And if we could just go up and to the right. That's perfect right there.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: On the top right-hand corner of the screen, can you tell us what that purple box is -- or rather, let me just ask you: Is that Cer that's indicated on the right-hand side of the screen?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Most probably, it's Cer, but I don't really see from here.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. And the box in the middle, the purple box in the middle of the screen a little bit just below the centre, does that represent Gucevo?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: The line that goes from Cer to the left and downwards, it's Gucevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And the line to the left and downwards from Gucevo, that purple line, does that go down to Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And what's indicated in this map as you've seen it, for these particular radio relay paths, those are the same paths that existed in July of 1995, right?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I'm done with this map.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Now, let me ask you, in July of 1995, who was the chief of communications for the Main Staff?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: In 1995, the chief of communications at the Main Staff was Colonel Prole.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. And if you recall, what was the code-name or the code that was used to identify Pribicevac in June and July of 1995?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: I don't know by heart. I would need to -- I think it's Ozren. That's what Mr. Petrusic asked me, secret code-names.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And you don't have a recollection at this time as to what the secret code-name was for Pribicevac; is that right?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Now, as chief of communications for the Drina Corps, how was it that you were able to establish communications in July or June 1995 with the 10th Sabotage Unit or Detachment?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: I don't recall that.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Would it have been through a radio relay communication or would it have been through a direct-wire communication? Can you tell us that?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember at all that we established communications with the 10th Sabotage Detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. And in relation to the communications network that was set up, that is, the radio relay routes that went from Vlasenica to Zvornik, through Veliki Zep, Cer, Gucevo, et cetera, was it the case that those communications could be listened to in Serbia and Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Well, they could be monitored on those hubs.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And the hubs in particular, you're talking about the ones that are situated in Yugoslavia, Cer, right, and Gucevo? Is that right?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Cer and Gucevo, right.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. I want to show you a document. It's 65 ter -- well, before I get to that, I'm sorry, let me ask you: Did you have or were there VRS members at those particular hubs in Serbia in and around July and August of 1995?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember having any communication with them. There was no need.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Let me show you 65 ter 2821. What you should have in front of you is an order for the communications established in relation to Operation Stit that you indicated was on this map. Now, before, I asked you some questions about interception capabilities, and you told me that at the switchboard you need a spy in order to intercept communications along the RRU-800 paths. I just want to direct your attention to paragraph numbered 5 to this document in front of you. That should be at the bottom of your first page. It talks about communication information protection. It says, in part: "I strictly forbid the relaying of confidential information through means of communication without the use of cryptographic data protection devices, in general, and special cryptographic protection documents." It then says at number 2 under that paragraph: "Anti--electronic protection. "The enemy are in a position to monitor and jam our command and control communications. In planning and using communications, make certain that besides this prescribed tactical and technical measures of protection, general and special protection of documents for cryptographic protection are used." If I could just refer you now to the next page of that document, that appears to reflect your signature. That is your signature, isn't it, Mr. Blagojevic?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: It's my signature, but I didn't find what you were saying.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Well, I'm sorry. Let me refer you to paragraph numbered 5. It should be right on the front -- the first page in front of you, and it's number 2 in that paragraph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It is right in the middle of that page.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: It's at the bottom, I'm sorry, the very bottom of that page.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You've had a chance to read that, Mr. Blagojevic?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And it is the case that when you were preparing this operation, Stit 1995, that the enemy was in a position to monitor and jam your command and control communications, as you've indicated in this document, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the witness responded; however, this document does not have a date, and I would really appreciate it if my learned friend could tell us to what period this document relates. Is it linked to Stit or Proboj or what operation? The document has no date.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: In his last question, Mr. Vanderpuye referred to this Stit Operation 1995. However, does the document have a date?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: The document does not have a date; however, the document -- I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: It's part of a November 1995 collection of documents that was received in connection -- that is related to the Operation Stit; the map, communication codes, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Sorry. May we see any document indicating this date, November 1995?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I don't understand what the objection is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's a collection --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Any connected with this document which --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But he's telling you. Usually, we don't doubt what the counsel says in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: That's all right with me. The only issue is that I've put it to the witness specifically whether or not that condition existed at that time. And he answered that it did, that they did have information that the enemy was able to jam and monitor the command and control structures in 1995.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, let's not lose more time.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: The witness didn't answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. But he has to answer the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And Ms. Stewart has just informed me that the entire defence plan is 65 ter 128, and this document comes from that defence plan.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And the question to you, Mr. Blagojevic, was the following: And it is the case that when you were preparing this operation, Stit 1995, that the enemy was in a position to monitor and jam your command and control communications as you have indicated in this document, isn't it? Could you give us an answer to that question, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You know what? Such measures in para 2, as I indicated, anti-electronic protection always proceed from the assumption that the enemy is able to do that. Whether it's needed or not, measures of anti-electronic protection are envisaged. But we have had confirmation that they had been listening in on us from 1992 and 1993 in unsecured communications. That's why this is written.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. So you're saying that it's in there because it's an assumption; is that right, Mr. Blagojevic?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: It's an assumption and it's for prevention purposes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Since you say it's an assumption, let me direct you to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Listen, I don't want to interfere, but an assumption or knowledge? Because the last part of his previous answer was: "But we have had confirmation that they had been listening in on us from 1992 and 1993 in unsecured communications. That's why this is written."

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: With respect to what's stated in the document I've just shown you, 1995, was it an assumption in that document that the enemy was able to monitor and jam your command and control functions, communications?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: This thing here is a preventive measure in the order based on past experience, but it doesn't apply to all communications. It applies only to unsecured communications, especially radio ones, on a lower tactical level: Brigades-battalions; battalion-company; company-platoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Now, with respect to the RRU-800 communications that you were talking about, it's a fact, Mr. Blagojevic, isn't it, that the security of those radio relay paths is only as good as the personnel operating that equipment? That's true, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And for all the rules and security that you've been referring to, the bottom line is that if those rules weren't followed, the result would be that the enemy would have the information that we've seen in this case, through radio intercepts. That's true too, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And, in fact --

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: That's why here -- may I finish?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: That's why here, in point 1, it's indicated: "Protect speech by using general documents of encryption and by using equipment such as KZU 31 and 63."

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And, in fact, Mr. Blagojevic, that wasn't always done and that's what Drago Nikolic is talking about in 22nd April 1993 --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Sorry. But --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: -- the translation is not complete. If the witness could repeat his answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Blagojevic. Thank you, Mr. Zivanovic. The interpreters couldn't get the last part of your answer. What we have is the following: "That's why here, in point 1, it's indicated: 'Protect speech by using general documents of encryption and by using equipment such as KZU 31 and 63.'" What was the rest of your answer that we have missed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, even that is not correct. The devices were speech protection KZU 63 and KZU 61.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. But do you wish to add anything to that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And then it goes: "Written information should be protected with devices KZU 41, KZU 31 ..."

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. Blagojevic, it is the case that those security measures that you've just outlined and many other security measures that were necessary to your function, as the chief of communication for the Drina Corps were not followed?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: You are referring to the information provided by Mr. Nikolic from the Zvornik Brigade dating back to 1993; however, this was done in 1995. And it is based on this that you heard from Mr. Nikolic and other who were abreast of the situation, and it is because of them that I ever drafted such order.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. So you drafted the orders on the recommendations concerning the security of the communications system based upon things such as the document that I introduced you to that was written by Drago Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. And that document indicates the commanding officers were prone to negligence, people stayed on the wire too long, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: It is very possible that this is correct, but I was not standing next to every commander or their deputy. All I did was my job, and there is only as much as one can do.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Let me show you 65 ter 2352; it's an illustration.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: The English on the screen should be A, and the witness should have in front of him C.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: This is a communication, 20th of April, 1995, at 1910 hours, on a frequency of 822 megahertz, which as you know corresponds to the frequency range of an RRU-800 device. This conversation is a conversation between - the evidence is in this case - between Lieutenant-Colonel Popovic and Second Lieutenant Drago Nikolic. And it's a long conversation, but I'll tell you what it says in part.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this document doesn't show that there is a conversation between Mr. Nikolic and Popovic. It says here Palma and Nikolic, but we cannot know whether this person is actually Drago Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But that's a submission. It's a proposition that the Mr. Vanderpuye is making to the witness. So let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: In this conversation, Mr. Blagojevic, you can see that there is communication with Zlatar, and if you could tell us what that is -- or let me ask you this: Is it the code-name for the Drina Corps command?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Zlatar is the code-name for the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And you know who Lieutenant-Colonel Popovic is, right?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. And he's a person that's likely to be found at Zlatar or through Zlatar?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And this is a conversation between one Nikolic and Lieutenant-Colonel Popovic, and it talks about somebody named Jovicic and that Jovicic has sent some volunteers. And as you can see from the conversation, because I'm not going to read the whole thing - it is a fairly long conversation - it talks about these volunteers being sent up there and a response that maybe they should be tested, or there's some question about whether or not they are legitimate volunteers. You see that?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Let me give you another example of a communication that was intercepted among high-ranking officers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. Mr. Zivanovic, do you have re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: How long?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't believe that I could complete my re-examination today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So are there arrangements in place to have this witness available tomorrow?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: There's about a half-hour left, and I can wrap this up hopefully in five minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What do you mean a half-hour left?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I looked at the clock the wrong way. You're right. I don't know whether --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I just want to confirm that there are arrangements for this witness to be present again tomorrow and whether arrangements have been -- how can we know that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Then we can continue, but I would ask you to wrap-up. We are not going to accept any further wrong indications. You indicated one hour and, it's already past the one hour, well past the one hour. So please conclude your cross.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. Blagojevic, I would like to show you 65 ter 1160.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: The English is A and the B/C/S which you should have is C.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I've just put a document to the witness. I'm sorry, Mr. President. It's 65 ter 1160, and it should be coming up in the e-court. A is the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: This is an intercept, sir, where you have two participants. And if you look towards the bottom of the -- towards the bottom of the page in front of you, this is 14th of July, 1995. You can see that these two individuals are discussing information, and one of them is actually complaining that sensitive information is being leaked by the other person on the -- by the other speaker on the end of this conversation. And in particular in this conversation, you see P says: "You're worse than the one who put me through to you. He says the rank, the name, the last name. The only thing missing is the date of birth, current location, and what his intentions are." In fact, Mr. Blagojevic, it is the case that this is precisely the types of things that were going on with relation to communications conducted over the radio relay system; and you're aware of that, aren't you?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: This is a radio relay communication, and it doesn't say that everything was recorded in both directions. They could not record both the emission and reception frequencies regardless of the feature. It is incredible that they did.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You find it incredible that two people are talking on an intercept and one is complaining about the other leaking information? You find that incredible, Mr. Blagojevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I don't know if you have an objection, but if you do I'd like to hear it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: He has answered the question. Let's move to the next question. You have already exceeded the one hour by 36 minutes, Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm not sure the witness saw the same document as the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't know. I mean, I wouldn't be able to tell.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: In the English text that we have on e-court, it is the document that he has been referred to.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, no. But in the -- yes. You're probably right, you're probably right, but we want to make sure. Mr. Blagojevic, the document that you have in front of you over there which you were given, what is its reference number at the top or the bottom?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1160C.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Then we are fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. Blagojevic, you were on duty on the 13th July 1995; that's correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And, in fact, you were the duty officer for the Drina Corps command on that day; is that true?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Take a look at 65 ter 3011, please.

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: 3011? What document did you say then? We've got it.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. If you look at line 14, that's your name, and you're on duty on the 13th of July as the duty officer?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And, in that position, you would have been aware of all the events that were occurring in and around the corps on that day?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, on all important details.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And you were present at the corps command on the 13th of July in the evening when General Krstic became the commander of the corps --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye, you have to finish your cross-examination in five minutes. Then you have not more than 15 minutes to finish your re-direct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I'll comply with your guidance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I think you would have been present at the corps at the time that General Krstic became the corps commander; is that right?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And at that point, who became the Chief of Staff?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Colonel Svetozar Andric was standing in for the Chief of Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. If I could, I would like to show you 65 ter 1134B.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: This will be the last document I show this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: While that's getting loaded, Mr. Blagojevic, can you tell us who the chief of operations was at the Drina Corps on 13 July?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: I'm not sure. I don't know. I've forgotten his name, but Obrad Vitic took over from him a few days later. He was a colonel by rank.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. With respect to this last document, my question is to you, Mr. Blagojevic - I'm going to read to you part of it - where it says: "C: Hey, wait. Someone else will talk to you first until I find Krstic for you. Here, you have Zlatar on the line. "Hello." And it says: "Hello, Krsmanovic speaking. "Hey Krle." Then it says: "Yes. One boss from the other batch so they can turn to the other side?" Then it says --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, one moment. Ms. Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. There's no date on the document. What's the date of this conversation, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: 13 July.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Frequency is 785, and the time is 1110 hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Blagojevic -- or your question, actually.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: It says: "One bus from the other batch so they can turn to the other side." And it says: "Dammit, Nedo. Over there, you know, for those in Batkovic, that means the job is being done over there now? "No, no. The job is being done, but one batch will go there." And it says: "One batch." At it says: "From Sekovici." And it continues. Do you have any idea what job it is talking about, and are you the Nedo that is indicated in this intercept, Mr. Blagojevic?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: I am a Nedo, but this is not a name; this is just an expression. Nedo is part of the expression: goddammit. This is not a name.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: This is a communication that went to the Drina Corps on the 13th of July the day that you were the duty officer, is it not?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This is your last question, Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: What job are they talking about?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: I was a duty officer, and Krsmanovic was the logistics chief of the transportation services. That's on the third floor, and the operations centre where I was on duty was on the first floor. So I really could not be in the picture there, nor did I know what the conversation was all about. I've never seen this conversation before.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Blagojevic. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you for your indulgence, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Zivanovic. I saw you standing, Madam Faveau.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness has answered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm really not in position to reduce my re-examination in next five minutes. I identified more than --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Fifteen minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Fifteen minutes. Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You think you will finish in 15 minutes?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I'll do my best to do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You always do, so let's try it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Blagojevic, I would like to ask you a couple of questions with regard to the Prosecutor's examination -- cross-examination. He asked you about the changes in the frequencies. Since we did not see among the documents all the frequency plans, when you were talking about the changes of the frequencies, what radio relay devices did you have in mind? You provided us with several when you were talking about that, so which ones did you have in mind in particular?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: This primarily referred to the radio relay devices RRU-1, because they are much easier to interfere with and listen to, much easier than an RRU-800.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Let's now look the document that the Prosecutor showed you, which is 2823.

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I think I'm --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. 1150 is the number.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Go on.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: The Prosecutor asked you whether a duplex connection at the switchboard give you possibility to hear both collocutors. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And you said --

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, affirmative.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Does the fact that both collocutors can be heard at the switchboard allow those who are listening in the conversation to hear both collocutors?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: No. And that's what I said to the Prosecutor when he was examining me. It's impossible because those who are listening are listening to the radio relay route, and they can only listen to one direction and that's the direction going towards the intercepters. And they can't hear the other collocutor, the other side.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: So to cut a long story short, when you have two collocutors in a conversation, are you saying that only one of them could be heard, not the other?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Precisely. The other person would be impossible to hear.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now look at 3412, please; it's a Prosecution document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you see in this document that the radio relay route, one of those routes used by the Drina Corps, was inoperative.

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: No, that's what I said to the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, is it usual to perform regular maintenance of these routes, radio relay routes, even when they are in operation?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: It's a reasonable question. We do regular checks and servicing and maintenance.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Just to add to my previous question about duplex devices, if during a conversation you could hear both collocutors, would that mean that two devices were used from both sides for eavesdropping?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: That could mean that they had one device in the territory of the Federation and the other device in the territory of Serbia; that's the only way.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: One more thing. You have seen this. In this document, while we're looking at it, let's finish with it, it says: "Repair and put into working order the radio relay route with 120 channels," and the routes are indicated. Are they in the area of the Drina Corps?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: They are on Veliki Zep-Cer and Veliki Zep-Stara -- Strazbenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: No. You didn't understand my question. Let's look at this document from the 25th of November, 1993. The second paragraph begins with the words: "Please send the same team to VRS to put into working order the 120-channel radio relay routes, number," and then you see the routes. Is one of these routes in the area of the Drina Corps?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: None of the routes indicated in this paragraph is in the area of the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we just look at another exhibit, 3425, Prosecution exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm ready.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me to whom this document was sent?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: It was sent --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: If you can't, say you can't.

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: I don't see here; it only says to the organ for other affairs, intelligence and security affairs.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Have you seen this document before?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: I have not, nor was there any need to submit it to me, because it was supposed to go to intelligence and security.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Just repeat, can you tell from which document to which unit it was sent?

utterances.speaker: NEDO BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: You can't see that. You can't see to which unit. You can see who wrote it and you see to which organ it is being sent, but not to which unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Blagojevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: No further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. I think you're standing up in vain, Mr. Petrusic. If you're asking to put questions, we are not going to allow it. Yes?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I had no intention to ask questions, but I would like to take up document 338, while the witness is here, to ask the witness to sign it and put today's date because certain changes have been made to the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Yes, thank you, Mr. Petrusic. Madam Registrar over there, could you take care of that, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [via Videolink] Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And for the record, we can see the witness hesitating.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What date is it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Today is the 17th of June.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Blagojevic, I wish to thank you very much for having been patient with us and stayed there all this time, and for having accepted to give evidence; and on behalf of the Trial Chamber, I wish you a safe journey to wherever you are going. Thank you. We'll do the exhibits tomorrow morning. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
